paragraphs: He is mentioned in Shabbat 139b, Chullin 22b: 'Yaakov Karcha taught'; and in Eruvin 86a: Abaye said, 'Yaakov Karchinaah taught' (and in Dikdukei Soferim, 'Karcha').[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: קלט:/כב:/פו. give Shabbat 139b/Chullin 22b/Eruvin 86a by convention, without new named verification.
The source prints דק״ם, interpreted contextually as Dikdukei Soferim; this is not a repair to דק״ס or a verified edition identification.

Karcha/Karchinaah remain transliterated different forms without etymology or identity binding. תני means recited/taught with Yaakov as subject, not an imperative. Abaye is the explicit reporter in Eruvin, and no personal rabbinic titles are supplied.
